examples.en: Hot lava flows out of the volcano.
Lava becomes hard rock when it cools.
Jeju Island has caves formed from lava.
There is a tour where you can see lava up close.
The whole village disappeared because of the lava.
In the movie, the main character crosses over lava.

explain: 화산에서 나온 뒤의 뜨거운 액체 상태의 돌은 '용암', 땅속에 있을 때는 '마그마'라고 해요. 식어서 굳으면 '화산암'이 돼요. '용암이 흐르다', '용암이 분출하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: Lava flows slowly down the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '용암'과 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common partner phrase of 용암.

phrases.en: Lava suddenly erupted from the volcano.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세게 터져 나오는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for lava bursting out with force.

phrases.en: Magma is hot rock under the ground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅속에 있을 때는 '마그마', 밖으로 나오면 '용암'이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Underground it is 마그마; once it comes out, it is 용암.

explain_en: Once out of the volcano, the hot liquid rock is '용암' (lava); while still underground it is '마그마' (magma). When it cools and hardens it becomes '화산암'. Common uses are '용암이 흐르다' and '용암이 분출하다'.

examples.en: Thunder rumbled in the distance.
The sky rumbled, and then the rain poured down.

examples.ko: 밤새 우르릉 소리가 들려서 잠을 설쳤어요.
examples.en: I heard a rumbling sound all night and slept badly.

examples.ko: 우르릉 쾅 하는 소리에 아이가 놀라서 울었어요.
examples.en: The child was startled by the rumble and bang and cried.

examples.ko: 산 너머에서 우르릉 소리가 점점 가까워져요.
examples.en: The rumbling from beyond the mountain is getting closer.

examples.ko: 기차가 우르릉 하고 다리 위를 지나갔어요.
examples.en: The train rumbled across the bridge.

explain: 천둥이나 큰 기계, 기차가 내는 낮고 무거운 소리를 흉내 내는 말이에요. '우르릉 쾅쾅'처럼 '쾅'과 함께 쓰는 일이 많아요.

phrases.example: 우르릉 쾅쾅 천둥이 쳐서 잠이 깼어요.
phrases.en: Thunder rumbled and crashed, and I woke up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천둥소리를 흉내 낼 때 가장 많이 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form for imitating thunder.

phrases.en: A rumbling sound comes from far away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낮고 무거운 소리가 들릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a low, heavy sound is heard.

phrases.en: The train rumbled past.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 이어질 때 반복해서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Repeated when the sound continues.

explain_en: It imitates the low, heavy sound of thunder, big machines or trains. It is often paired with '쾅' as in '우르릉 쾅쾅'.

examples.en: The crops in the greenhouse were wiped out by the cold wave.
An epidemic spread and the chickens nearly all died.

examples.ko: 게임 속 우리 팀이 순식간에 전멸하고 말았어요.
examples.en: Our team in the game got wiped out in an instant.

examples.ko: 병충해 때문에 올해 사과 농사가 전멸하다시피 했어요.
examples.en: Because of pests, this year's apple farming was practically wiped out.

examples.ko: 전멸한 부대의 소식은 끝내 전해지지 않았어요.
examples.en: No news ever came of the unit that was wiped out.

examples.ko: 이 섬의 토종 새는 전멸해서 지금은 볼 수 없어요.
examples.en: The native birds of this island died out, so you cannot see them now.

explain: 사람이나 동물, 작물, 군대가 하나도 남지 않고 다 없어질 때 써요. '멸종하다'는 한 종류의 생물이 지구에서 사라질 때 쓰고, 전멸하다는 한 곳이나 한 무리가 다 사라질 때 써요. 게임에서 팀원이 모두 죽었을 때도 일상적으로 말해요. 건물이나 물건에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: The army wiped out the enemy unit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가가 다 없앴다는 뜻으로, 하는 쪽을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means someone wiped everything out, focusing on the doer.

phrases.en: Our team was wiped out in the game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 게임에서 모두 죽었을 때 대화에서도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used in conversation when everyone dies in a game.

phrases.en: The farm's crops are on the verge of being wiped out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거의 다 없어질 위기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a state of near total loss.
phrases.en_equiv: on the verge of being wiped out

explain_en: Use it when people, animals, crops or an army are all gone with none left. '멸종하다' is for a whole species vanishing from the earth, while '전멸하다' is for one place or one group being completely lost. People also say it in games when the whole team is dead. It is not used for buildings or objects.

examples.en: A cold wave advisory has been issued for tomorrow morning.
The flight was canceled because of the typhoon advisory.

examples.ko: 산불 주의보가 내려서 등산을 못 해요.
examples.en: A wildfire advisory is in effect, so we can't hike.

examples.ko: 폭염 주의보가 끝날 때까지 집에 있었어요.
examples.en: I stayed home until the heat advisory ended.
An advisory text message came, so I took an umbrella.
When an advisory is issued, school ends early.

explain: 주의보는 '경보'보다 한 단계 약한 경고예요. 보통 주의보 다음에 상황이 심해지면 경보가 나와요. '호우 주의보', '한파 주의보'처럼 앞에 날씨를 붙이고, '주의보가 내리다/발령되다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: A heavy snow advisory was issued for Gangwon Province.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주의보가 처음 나올 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when an advisory is first issued.

phrases.en: The advisory was lifted in the afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨가 나아져서 주의보가 끝날 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when the advisory ends because the weather improves.

phrases.en: There was a heavy rain advisory, so I didn't go out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비가 많이 올 때 내리는 주의보예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the advisory issued for heavy rain.

explain_en: A 주의보 is one step weaker than a 경보 (warning). If conditions get worse after a 주의보, a 경보 follows. Put the weather before it, as in 호우 주의보 or 한파 주의보, and say 주의보가 내리다 or 주의보가 발령되다.

examples.en: Our house is heated with natural gas.

examples.ko: 천연가스 가격이 올라서 요금이 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: The price of natural gas went up, so the bill was high.
This bus runs on natural gas.
Natural gas pollutes the air less than coal.

examples.ko: 한국은 천연가스를 다른 나라에서 많이 사 와요.
examples.en: Korea buys a lot of natural gas from other countries.
The news said the supply of natural gas decreased.

explain: 천연가스는 땅속에서 나오는 불에 타는 기체예요. 집에서 요리하고 난방할 때 쓰는 '도시가스'도 대부분 천연가스로 만들어요. 줄여서 'LNG'라고도 하는데, 이건 액체로 만든 천연가스를 가리켜요.

phrases.en: Natural gas buses run in this city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천연가스로 움직이는 버스를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A bus that runs on natural gas.

phrases.en: The factory uses natural gas.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연료로 사용한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means using it as fuel.

phrases.en: Natural gas fees go up in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 난방에 쓰는 가스의 돈을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the cost of gas used for heating.

explain_en: 천연가스 is a flammable gas that comes out of the ground. The 도시가스 used for cooking and heating at home is mostly made from natural gas. It is also abbreviated LNG, which specifically means natural gas turned into liquid.

examples.ko: 이 새는 천연기념물로 지정돼서 잡으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: This bird is designated a natural monument, so you must not catch it.
Jeju Island has many natural monuments.
I went to the island to take pictures of a natural monument.
Is that tree a natural monument too?

examples.ko: 천연기념물은 함부로 만지거나 옮기면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not touch or move a natural monument carelessly.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 뒷산에도 천연기념물인 새가 살아요.
examples.en: A bird that is a natural monument lives on the hill behind my town too.

explain: 나라에서 보호하려고 지정한 동물, 식물, 지형 같은 자연물에 써요. 건물이나 유물은 '문화재'나 '국보'라고 하고, '천연기념물'은 자연 쪽이에요. '천연기념물 제○호'처럼 번호를 붙여 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: That tree was designated a natural monument.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라에서 보호 대상으로 정한다는 뜻의 대표적인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The typical usage meaning the state designates it as protected.

phrases.en: Protecting natural monuments is important.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자연을 지키는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about protecting nature.

phrases.example: 안내판에 천연기념물 제 몇 호인지 적혀 있어요.
phrases.en: The sign shows which number natural monument it is.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지정된 순서를 나타내는 번호를 붙여 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with a registration number.

explain_en: It is used for animals, plants and landforms that the state designates for protection. Buildings and relics are called '문화재' or '국보', while '천연기념물' is for natural things. People often add a number, like '천연기념물 제○호'.

examples.ko: 요즘 산 근처에 멧돼지가 출몰해서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: Wild boars have been showing up near the mountain lately, so we have to be careful.

examples.ko: 이 지역에는 밤마다 너구리가 출몰한다고 해요.
examples.en: They say raccoon dogs appear in this area every night.
Don't swim at beaches where jellyfish keep showing up.

examples.ko: 어젯밤 마을에 곰이 출몰했다는 소문이 돌아요.
examples.en: There's a rumor that a bear showed up in the village last night.
Do you want to go to the house that's said to be haunted?

examples.ko: 동물이 출몰하지 않도록 마을 입구에 울타리를 쳤어요.
examples.en: They put up a fence at the village entrance so animals wouldn't show up.

explain: 뉴스에서는 멧돼지, 해파리, 불법 차량처럼 반갑지 않은 것이 여기저기 나타날 때 많이 써요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '나타나다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: Don't go to areas where bears appear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험하거나 반갑지 않은 것이 나타나는 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for places where something unwelcome or dangerous shows up.

phrases.example: 등산로에 멧돼지 출몰 주의 안내가 있어요.
phrases.en: There is a notice on the trail warning of wild boars.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 뉴스에서 자주 보는 짧은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short phrase often seen on signs and in news.

phrases.en: A cat often shows up in front of my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같고 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, and more natural in daily speech.

explain_en: In the news it is often used for unwelcome things that keep turning up, like wild boars, jellyfish or illegal vehicles. In everyday talk people usually just say '나타나다'.

en: soil and sand; earth and sand (debris)

examples.en: It rained a lot, and soil and sand flowed down.
The road was blocked by earth and sand.
At the construction site, soil and sand are moved by truck.
We cleared the sediment piled up on the riverbed.

examples.ko: 토사 유출을 막기 위해 나무를 심었어요.
examples.en: We planted trees to stop soil from washing away.
I'm worried that soil will pour down the mountain slope.

explain: 토사는 산사태, 홍수, 공사 뉴스에서 자주 들어요. 일상에서는 '흙'과 '모래'를 따로 말하고, 둘이 섞인 덩어리를 한꺼번에 말할 때 토사를 써요. '토사 유출'처럼 붙어 나와요. 의학에서 구토와 설사를 뜻하는 '토사'(吐瀉)는 소리만 같고 한자가 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: Soil and sand leaked out from the construction site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공사나 비 때문에 흙과 모래가 흘러나갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is used when soil and sand flow out because of construction or rain.

phrases.en: Soil and sand poured down from the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산사태 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This often appears in landslide news.

phrases.en: They have been clearing the soil and sand from the road since morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쌓인 흙과 모래를 정리할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is used when removing piled-up soil and sand.

explain_en: 토사 is common in news about landslides, floods, and construction. In daily speech 흙 (soil) and 모래 (sand) are named separately, and 토사 is used for the mixed mass. It appears in phrases like 토사 유출. The medical 토사 (吐瀉), meaning vomiting and diarrhea, sounds the same but is written with different Chinese characters.

examples.en: Whales live by eating plankton.
There is a lot of plankton in seawater.

examples.ko: 플랑크톤은 너무 작아서 눈에 안 보여요.
examples.en: Plankton is so small that you can't see it.

examples.ko: 플랑크톤이 갑자기 늘면 물 색이 변하기도 해요.
examples.en: If plankton suddenly increases, the water's color can change.
In science class we looked at plankton under a microscope.
Small fish grow up eating plankton.

explain: 식물처럼 광합성을 하는 것은 '식물 플랑크톤', 움직이며 먹이를 먹는 것은 '동물 플랑크톤'이라고 해요. 과학 시간이나 바다, 환경 뉴스에 주로 나와요.

phrases.en: Phytoplankton make nutrients from sunlight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광합성을 하는 플랑크톤을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Plankton that photosynthesize.

phrases.en: Small fish eat zooplankton.
phrases.nuance_ko: 움직이며 먹이를 먹는 플랑크톤이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Plankton that move and feed on other organisms.

phrases.en: In spring, plankton increase in the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계절이나 환경에 따라 양이 변할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the amount changes with season or environment.

explain_en: The photosynthesizing kind is 식물 플랑크톤, and the kind that moves and feeds is 동물 플랑크톤. It mostly appears in science class and in news about the sea or the environment.

examples.ko: 도로 함몰 사고 때문에 길이 막혀요.
examples.en: The road is blocked because of a road collapse.
Residents were evacuated because of a sudden ground collapse.

examples.ko: 함몰이 일어난 곳 근처에는 가지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't go near the place where the collapse happened.

examples.ko: 시청이 함몰을 막으려고 지하 공사를 점검하고 있어요.
examples.en: City Hall is inspecting underground construction to prevent cave-ins.

examples.ko: 함몰은 비가 많이 온 뒤에 더 자주 생겨요.
examples.en: Cave-ins happen more often after heavy rain.
A safety line has been set up at the collapse site.

explain: 뉴스에서 '도로 함몰', '지반 함몰'처럼 앞에 땅이나 도로를 나타내는 말을 붙여 많이 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '땅이 꺼지다'라고 해요. 동사 '함몰되다'와 함께 알아 두세요.

phrases.en: Because of heavy rain, the road caved in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅이나 바닥이 아래로 푹 꺼지는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the ground or a surface sinking downward.

phrases.example: 이 지역은 함몰 위험이 있어서 조심해야 해요.
phrases.en: This area has a risk of caving in, so be careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안전 안내나 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation in safety notices and news.

phrases.example: 공사장 옆 땅이 꺼져서 길을 막았어요.
phrases.en: The ground next to the construction site sank, so they blocked the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '함몰'을 일상 대화에서 말하는 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easy everyday way to describe a 'hammol'.

explain_en: In the news it usually follows words like road or ground, as in '도로 함몰' and '지반 함몰'. In everyday talk people say '땅이 꺼지다'. Learn it together with the verb '함몰되다'.

examples.en: When the Earth gets warmer, sea levels rise.
The sun is rising above the sea surface.
The height of the sea surface differs slightly from sea to sea.
The news said rising sea levels are a problem.
The boat moves slowly close to the sea surface.

examples.ko: 섬이 해수면보다 낮아서 홍수가 자주 나요.
examples.en: The island is lower than sea level, so floods happen often.

explain: 산 높이를 말할 때는 '해발 1,000미터'처럼 '해발'을 쓰고, 바닷물의 높이 변화를 말할 때는 '해수면'을 써요. 뉴스에서 '해수면 상승'이라는 말로 자주 들어요.

phrases.example: 해수면 상승 때문에 섬이 작아지고 있어요.
phrases.en: Because of rising sea levels, the island is getting smaller.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in the news.

phrases.example: 이 도시는 해수면보다 낮아서 물이 잘 차요.
phrases.en: This city is below sea level, so it floods easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅의 높이를 바다와 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when comparing the height of land with the sea.

phrases.en: At low tide, the sea level goes down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바닷물 높이가 낮아질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the water height drops.

explain_en: For the height of a mountain, Korean says 해발 1,000미터. For changes in the height of the sea, it uses 해수면. You hear it often in the news as 해수면 상승.

examples.en: The firewood is burning brightly in the fireplace.

examples.ko: 불길이 활활 번지기 전에 빨리 119에 전화하세요.
examples.en: Call 119 quickly before the fire spreads and blazes up.
When the charcoal blazes up, put the meat on.
The fervor of the cheering blazed in the stadium.

examples.ko: 종이를 던지자 불에 활활 타 버렸어요.
examples.en: When I threw the paper in, it went up in flames.

examples.ko: 바람이 불자 불꽃이 더 활활 일어났어요.
examples.en: When the wind blew, the flames rose even higher.

explain: 불이 기운차게 크게 타오르는 모양을 말해서 주로 '타다', '타오르다'와 함께 써요. 열정이나 분노가 세게 일어나는 것을 불에 빗대어 말할 때도 있어요. 연기나 김이 조용히 오르는 모양은 '모락모락'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The bonfire blazed all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '타다'보다 불이 위로 크게 솟는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stronger than 타다, giving the feeling of flames rising high.

phrases.en: We built a roaring fire with firewood at the campsite.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불을 크게 일으킬 때 짝으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with making a big fire.

phrases.example: 그는 가슴에 활활 타오르는 열정이 있어요.
phrases.en: He has a blazing passion in his heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 열정이나 분노가 센 것을 불에 빗대어 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Compares strong passion or anger to fire.

explain_en: It describes a fire burning large and vigorously, and mostly goes with '타다' or '타오르다'. It can also compare strong passion or anger to fire. For steam or smoke rising quietly, Koreans say '모락모락'.
